Result now: backups are still happening in the basement drain after a few days, kitchen sink still slow, and they left a small leak at a cleanout they opened.

<action type="say">
Here’s a message you can send to North Shore Plumbing & Drain (email or text). Adjust any details as needed:

---

Subject: Request for Full Refund – Unresolved Main Line and Kitchen Sink Issues

To whom it may concern,

I am writing regarding the recent plumbing service at my property at 1842 Elmwood Ave, Buffalo, NY 14207, on or around December 1, 2025. Your technician was hired to:
- Clear a clogged main line, and  
- Fix a slow‑draining kitchen sink.

Within a few days of the visit, the same problems returned and new issues appeared:
- Backups are still occurring in the basement floor drain.  
- The kitchen sink remains slow‑draining.  
- There is now a small leak at the cleanout that your technician opened.

I called the next day to report these issues and was told the system “just needs time,” and that you would not return without charging another trip fee. Given that:
- The original problems were not resolved, and  
- A new leak was created at the cleanout,

I consider the service to be incomplete and not performed with reasonable care and skill.

I am therefore requesting a full refund of the amount paid for this service. Please confirm in writing within 7 calendar days how and when you will issue the refund.

If we cannot resolve this directly, I will have to pursue other options, including disputing the charge with my bank/credit card company and filing complaints with appropriate consumer protection and licensing authorities.

I prefer to resolve this matter amicably and promptly. Please let me know your response by [insert a date 7 days from now].

Sincerely,  
Tom Kowalski  
1842 Elmwood Ave  
Buffalo, NY 14207  
Phone: 716‑555‑3928  
Email: tom.kowalski@buffalony.gov

---

If they refuse or don’t respond:

1) Dispute with your bank/card
- Collect: the invoice, any texts/emails, notes of your call (dates/times), and photos/videos of the ongoing backups, slow sink, and leaking cleanout.
- When you contact your bank, clearly say that the work did not fix the issues, a new leak was introduced, and the company refused to return without an extra fee.

2) File complaints
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) in your area.  
- Your state/city consumer protection office and any plumbing licensing board (if they are licensed).

If you tell me how you paid (card, check, etc.) and roughly when, I can help you phrase exactly what to say to your bank for a dispute call or online claim.</action>
